newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU gas oil stocks seen down slightly in December.
newsitem.headline: EU gas oil stocks seen down slightly in December.

text.p: European Union stock figures for December to be released on Monday are expected to show a modest draw in gas oil, the product attracting most market attention, analysts said.
"There will likely be some small impact from the cold at the end of December, but there's still scope for them (gas oil stocks) to remain in the normal range," said Geoff Pyne, energy analyst at UBS.
"We see (gas oil stocks) coming down in December to something like last year's level," said Cindy Poynter of oil consultants Bonner and Moore.

Some analysts believe the figures will have to be dramatic to draw attention away from the recent spell of cold weather. The deep freeze and a resultant surge of gas oil demand are likely to have had a limited impact, because the cold only hit in at the very end of December.
"Unless there's a big draw, you could almost disregard December. The January figures are likely to be more interesting," said Leslie Owens of Petroleum Economics.
However, analysts are already assessing the ramifications of the recent freeze.
"We're showing in general, for the period November-January, that we will be about three to four days of supply below normal...It's something to be concerned about," says Poynter.
But gas oil shortages are unlikely with prolonged cold weather, say some.
"It only looks like a precarious supply situation if the cold weather continues," said Pyne.
Through summer and autumn, Euroil figures showed a substantial year-on-year shortfall of middle distillate stocks, rapid refinery throughput in November redressed the balance.
The November figures, revealing a middle distillate build of 2.55 million barrels, or 0.9 percent, to 295.73 million barrels surprised a number in the oil markets and introduced a bearish tinge.
Although middle distillate stocks remain the front line figure, some analysts urge traders at least to glance at the crude stocks levels.
Renewed Iraqi exports will not yet have taken effect, but a steady growth of North Sea output may have an impact on crude stocks.
"We normally see a small (crude) draw in December, but who knows this year," said Pyne.
The December figures may also provide some insight into the effect of the strike at French oil refiners which ended in the middle of the month.
"I wouldn't expect to see a draw, but the strike kept Europe as tight as it is ever going to get.
The Euroilstock report of the 14 countries of the European Union, without Sweden, will be published on Monday at 1400 GMT.
